en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Highlands, Monmouth County, New Jersey, 1907, Sheet 88

canvas-01-1.description: The main map of printed sheet 85 covers the northern end of Highlands between Bay Avenue and the Shrewsbury River, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with northwest at the top of the page. Bay Avenue runs down the left side of the sheet; the cross streets Atlantic, Cedar, Valley Avenue, Miller, East North and Cornwell run from it toward the river, and 4th Street, 5th Street and Point run parallel to Bay Avenue. Holly cuts diagonally from Atlantic to the corner of Cedar and 4th Street, and a short unnamed lane runs between 4th and 5th Streets north of Miller. The blocks are filled with small frame dwellings and the seasonal accommodation of a summer resort: summer houses, boarding houses and named cottages (Central Cottage, Young's Cottage, Emerald Cottage, Horse Shoe Cottage, Scherf Cottage, Riverside Cottage), the Sea Side Club, the Grand View Hotel, the Neptune House and a hotel at Miller and Point. Firemen's Hall stands on Valley Avenue near Bay Avenue, and St. Andrew's Episcopal church sits at Valley Avenue and 5th Street. Stores, a barber, a drug store and a hotel line Miller Street near Bay Avenue. Along the river shore are fish houses, a clam house, shanties, a bulkhead and a stretch marked private property. The far right of the page is cut off by a heavy border: above it the sheet carries the small-scale key map of the town and its population and fire-service note, which are not part of this map, and below it an inset of Bay Avenue south of the sheet edge (part 2). Street widths of 35 to 50 feet and many lot numbers are lettered.
notes: Valley Avenue here is today Valley Street.
Point is today Shrewsbury Avenue (the detected junctions with Miller and North Street fit it to under 1 m).
Cedar and 4th Street meet Holly at one corner, as in OpenStreetMap today.
Cornwell and the eastern end of East North are lettered 'not opened'.
5th Street is drawn about 20 ft wide and does not continue to Miller; the 5th Street / Valley Avenue junction was detected off the drawn street and rejected.

Printed sheet 85 (canvas labelled Overview). Scale 60 ft to an inch, drawn with northwest at the top (north to the upper right). Bay Av, Atlantic, Holly, Cedar, Valley Av, Miller, E. and W. North, Cornwell, 4th St, 5th St, Point St, Shrewsbury River. Two parts: 1 main map; 2 inset at the lower right (Bay Av between Cornwell and Jackson, east side) behind a heavy border. The upper right holds the town key map (sheets 70-72, 85-89, Water Witch Park) at a small scale and the town's population and fire-service note: not georeferenced, left out of the mask.

canvas-01-2.description: A small inset at the lower right of printed sheet 85, separated from the main map by a heavy border, showing the stretch of Bay Avenue in Highlands that lies just beyond the bottom edge of the main map, from Cornwell to Jackson. It is drawn at the same scale, 60 feet to an inch, and with Bay Avenue running straight down the page as on the main map. Only the east side of Bay Avenue is drawn: a drug store at the corner of Cornwell, and otherwise empty ground. The sheet numbers 85 and 86 printed inside it mark where the area drawn on sheet 86 begins, and the west side of the avenue is left blank because it belongs to that sheet. Jackson is lettered 'not opened' east of Bay Avenue. The inset was placed from the two junctions it shows, Bay Avenue with Cornwell and with Jackson, which lie about 80 m apart, so its placement rests on a short baseline.
notes: Jackson is lettered 'not opened' east of Bay Avenue; it is Jackson Street today.
Placed by a two-point helmert transformation from Bay Avenue / Cornwell Street and Bay Avenue / Jackson Street; low confidence.

sheet-86.description: Sheet 86 covers the western and hillside part of Highlands south of Bay Avenue, drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned a quarter turn against sheet 85, so that Bay Avenue runs along the top edge. Valley Avenue (lettered 'not opened') runs down the left edge, Miller down the middle and West North at the upper right; 2nd Street runs from Valley Avenue toward Miller below the Bay Avenue blocks, and Navesink Avenue and Highland Avenue cross the sheet lower down. In the lower part Woodland leaves Highland Avenue just west of Miller, and South Peak and Bay branch off toward the southeast, with a curving road lettered 'Road' and 'Woodland' along the bottom edge. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet from side to side between 2nd Street and Navesink Avenue, with a watchman's box at Miller; two ice ponds lie beside it, and the top of the high bank and a ravine are drawn south of the line. Commercial buildings and dwellings line Bay Avenue, including a fish market, a store house and a confectioner, with a Methodist Episcopal church on Miller. On Navesink and Highland Avenues are the public school, St. Mary's Roman Catholic church, the priest's house and St. Mary's Lyceum, with scattered cottages (Postal Cottage, Locust House, Lewis House, Grand View Cottage) on large lots. The names of Cornwell, Jackson and East North Streets are printed at the top edge where those streets leave the sheet.
notes: Valley Avenue is today Valley Street north of Shore Drive and Valley Avenue south of it.
West North is today North Street; South Peak is South Peak Street; Bay is Bay Street.
Woodland meets Highland Avenue about 60 ft west of Miller on the sheet; in OpenStreetMap the two junctions are 10 m apart, so Woodland was not used for control.
OpenStreetMap has Miller Street meeting Navesink Avenue at two nodes 32 m apart; the one in line with the drawn street was used.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey line drawn here is no longer a running railroad.

Scale 60 ft to an inch, turned 90 degrees against sheet 85 (Bay Av along the top). Bay Av, 2nd St, Valley Av (not opened), Miller, W. North, Navesink Av, Highland Av, Woodland, Woodland Road, Bay, S. Peak; C.R.R. of N.J. line across the middle, ice ponds, top of the high bank. One part.

sheet-87-1.description: The main map of sheet 87 covers the southeastern corner of Highlands where Bay Avenue, Navesink Avenue and Highland Avenue converge on the Shrewsbury River and the bridge to the beach, drawn at 60 feet to an inch. Bay Avenue enters at the upper left, meets Kay and then the junction with South Street, where Shrewsbury Avenue comes in from the north, and continues south as a narrower street. Navesink Avenue and Highland Avenue cross the lower left of the sheet and join near the bottom, from where Highland Avenue runs east to the wooden bridge and the draw bridge across the river. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs diagonally across the sheet past a passenger station and a freight house to the draw bridge, along the foot of a bluff. Industry and resort buildings fill the ground between the streets and the shore: the Christian Williams cement block factory, the Sea Side Grove cottages, Creighton's dancing pavilion and B. Creighton's hotel, the Summer Hotel, a beer bottling works, M. H. McGuire's boat house and the Twin Light Boat Club with piers into the river. Hotels and houses on Navesink and Highland Avenues include the Highland House, the Monmouth House and The Victoria. The upper right corner beyond a heavy border is a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Kay on this sheet runs from Bay Avenue in line with today's first block of Center Street and then Kay Street; the junction was matched to Bay Avenue / Center Street.
The junction of Bay Avenue, Shrewsbury Avenue and the street toward the river is today Bay Avenue / South Street and Shrewsbury Avenue / South Street; South Street is not lettered on the sheet.
Navesink Avenue south of its junction with Highland Avenue is today Portland Road; the old Navesink Avenue toward the bridge has been replaced by the NJ 36 approach.
Only four junctions survive on this part, so the lower half near the bridge is placed by extrapolation; medium confidence.

Scale 60 ft to an inch. Kay, Bay Av, Shrewsbury Av, Navesink Av, Highland Av, Jackson, Shrewsbury River; C.R.R. of N.J. line and station area, Christian Williams cement block works, Sea Side Grove cottages, Creighton dancing pavilion, Summer hotel, Water bridge. Two parts: 1 main map; 2 inset at the upper right behind a heavy border (Shrewsbury Av and Jackson with the Jackson Club, river on both sides).

sheet-87-2.description: An inset in the upper right of sheet 87, behind a heavy border, showing Shrewsbury Avenue in Highlands where Jackson meets it, at the same scale of 60 feet to an inch. Shrewsbury Avenue runs down the page as a 50 foot street with the river drawn close along its west side, and Jackson runs east from it to the shore. The ground east of the avenue is laid out in lots facing the water, with the Jackson Club and its outbuildings north of Jackson, the Barefoot Club and a few dwellings south of it, a boat club house at the top, and docks and a pier reaching into the Shrewsbury River on the east side. Lettering of the river appears on both sides of the inset. The inset is drawn north of the area of the main map, continuing Shrewsbury Avenue beyond the top edge of the sheet.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction (Jackson Street / Shrewsbury Avenue) with the scale and rotation of the main part of the sheet; low confidence.
Jackson is Jackson Street today and now ends at Shrewsbury Avenue.

Scale 60 ft to an inch. Kay, Bay Av, Shrewsbury Av, Navesink Av, Highland Av, Jackson, Shrewsbury River; C.R.R. of N.J. line and station area, Christian Williams cement block works, Sea Side Grove cottages, Creighton dancing pavilion, Summer hotel, Water bridge. Two parts: 1 main map; 2 inset at the upper right behind a heavy border (Shrewsbury Av and Jackson with the Jackson Club, river on both sides).

sheet-88.description: Sheet 88 covers the southern end of Highlands below Highland Avenue, between the hill toward the Navesink lighthouses and the Shrewsbury River, drawn at 60 feet to an inch. Highland Avenue curves in at the upper left and meets Navesink Avenue, which runs straight down the sheet, and the avenue then turns northeast toward the bridge. Bay Avenue runs down the right side above the river shore, and Hillside Road crosses the sheet from Navesink Avenue to Bay Avenue and beyond. The upper half is the hotel district of the resort: the Hotel Martin, the East View House with billiards room, ice house and gas machine, the Tuxedo Hotel by the river, Thompson's Hotel, Greason's Restaurant, Angus Cottage and other cottages, with a boat house on government property, piers and a steam boat dock along the shore and the top of a bluff between Navesink and Bay Avenues. The lower half is open hillside with a few large houses (J. Wheelock, Mrs. J. W. Webster, Hayden, F. C. Moore) and a borough line crossing it diagonally. A note gives the distance of about 900 feet to the lighthouse on the hill.
notes: Navesink Avenue on this sheet is today Portland Road; Bay Avenue here is today South Bay Avenue; Hillside Road is Hillside Avenue.
Today's Highland Avenue east of Portland Road to South Bay Avenue is not on the sheet.
Placed from three junctions only (an exact fit); the lower half of the sheet has no control.

Scale 60 ft to an inch. Highland Av, Navesink Av, Bay Av, Hillside Road, Shrewsbury River shore; Hotel Martin, East View House, Thompson's Hotel, Gregory's restaurant, Hotel; southern half sparse estates. One part.
